title: The maximal-index conjecture for sums of matrix entries from a probability vector
statement:
Let $p\in\mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ satisfy

$$
\sum_{i=1}^d p_i=1.
$$

Define matrices $a,g\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ by

$$
a_{ij}=\frac{p_i+p_j}{2},\qquad g_{ij}=\sqrt{p_i p_j}.
$$

Let $a_k^\downarrow$ and $g_k^\downarrow$ denote the $k$th largest entries of $a$ and $g$, respectively, and set

$$
A=\sum_{k=1}^{h(d)}a_k^\downarrow,\qquad G=\sum_{k=1}^{h(d)}g_k^\downarrow.
$$

**Maximal-index conjecture.** The maximal integer $h(d)$ for which $A+G\leq d$ holds for every probability vector $p$ is

$$
h(d)=2d-5.
$$

This conjecture concerns the sharp index in a bound arising from criteria for Markovian divisibility of linear maps. The supplied text gives no resolution or evidence establishing the claim, so its status remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.06666

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).
source_name: Matthias C. Caro and Benedikt Graswald, “Necessary Criteria for Markovian Divisibility of Linear Maps”, arXiv:2009.06666 (2022).
